blocks.title: Access Control Models and Least Privilege comparison
Access Control Models and Least Privilege exam shortcuts
items: Central policy and labels determine access.
Example: Secret-labeled data requires matching clearance.
The owner has discretion over permissions.
Example: A user shares a folder with a coworker.
Assign access to roles instead of individuals.
Example: All HR analysts receive the HR role.
Attributes are evaluated at access time.
Example: Finance access requires finance role + managed device + approved location.
Access only during business hours → TIME-OF-DAY RESTRICTION
The schedule itself is part of authorization.
Example: Contractor account works only from 8 AM to 6 PM.
User has more rights than necessary → LEAST PRIVILEGE
Example: Help desk user loses domain-admin access.
blocks.example: First determine whether the scenario is asking who the user is, what they can do, how they authenticate, or how privileged access should be controlled.

questions.q: A classified system grants access based on security labels and clearance levels controlled by central policy. Which model is this?
questions.explanation: Mandatory Access Control uses centrally enforced labels and classifications.

questions.q: A file owner chooses which coworkers can access a document. Which model is this?
questions.explanation: Discretionary Access Control allows the owner to decide who gets access.

questions.q: All HR analysts automatically receive the same permissions because they belong to the HR Analyst role. Which model is this?
questions.explanation: RBAC assigns permissions based on job roles.

questions.q: Access is allowed only when the user's department is Finance, the device is managed, and the request originates from an approved location. Which model is this?
questions.explanation: ABAC evaluates multiple attributes such as user, device, and location.

questions.q: A contractor account works only between 8 AM and 6 PM. Which control is this?
questions.explanation: Time-of-day restrictions constrain access based on schedule.

questions.q: A help desk employee has domain administrator rights even though the job does not require them. Which principle should be applied?
questions.explanation: Least privilege removes permissions that are not required for the job.
